newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Australia trade minister sees greater SAfrica ties.
newsitem.headline: Australia trade minister sees greater SAfrica ties.

text.p: Australia's trade minister and deputy prime minister, Tim Fischer, said on Tuesday South Africa's economic policies had boosted foreign investor confidence, which promised increased Australian investment.

Leading a business delegation at the start of a three-day visit to South Africa, Fischer said the economies of the two countries were undergoing a reform process that could bring them closer together.

"The economic reform processes that are actively being pursued in Australia and South Africa present many opportunities for our bilateral relationship," Fischer told a business function in the east coast port city of Durban.
He said trade was increasing between the two countries at a trend growth rate of 35 percent per annum since 1991.

"Even though Foreign Direct Investment inflows are slow at present, Australian businesses are willing to take the plunge and to participate with you in building a vibrant and prosperous South Africa."

Australia was also interested in the trade and investment opportunities emerging from trade liberalisation in the southern African economic bloc of the 12-member Southern African Development Community, he said.

Fischer said Australian companies had been opened up to the discipline of international competition by the reduction of Australia's general tariff rate to five percent across a majority of tariff lines.
The private sector had responded strongly and manufacturing and services now accounted for just over half of Australian exports of goods and services, he said.
Australian GDP growth for the 1997-98 financial year is forecast at 3.5 percent, while consumer price inflation is estimated at 1.75 percent compared to one percent for 1996-97.
Fischer will hold talks with South African Trade Minister Alec Erwin on Wednesday and Thursday in Pretoria as part of the first Joint Ministerial Commission.
